C++ Playground

Self-hosted C++ playground

A complete C++ toolchain running inside this tab. Clang 22.1.8, wasm-ld and libc++ are themselves WebAssembly binaries, so your code is compiled, linked and executed on your own machine. No server ever sees it, there are no accounts, and the page keeps working offline once it has loaded.

Run it yourself

This is free software and it is meant to be copied. Download the release archive, unpack it and run python serve.py — that is the whole installation.

⤓ Download the playground (.zip) Source on GitHub

Using it

  • Ctrl+Enter compiles and runs; Stop kills a runaway program.
  • Add headers and sources in Files; subdirectories work, and everything is built together.
  • Arguments becomes argv, quoted like a shell.
  • Programs block on std::cin and you type into the console; Ctrl+D ends input. Program input preloads text before that.
  • std::thread runs on real Web Workers over one shared memory. threads on auto adds -pthread only when your code needs it.
  • Download .zip in the toolbar exports your project with a buildable CMakeLists.txt.
  • Your files are kept in this browser's localStorage; Reset clears them.

Good to know

  • Interactive input and threads need a cross-origin isolated host (COOP/COEP). Where that is missing the playground says so and falls back.
  • Compiled programs have no networking, and hardware_concurrency() reports 1.
  • First load fetches ~35 MB of toolchain, then caches it.

MIT licensed. Clang, LLD and libc++ are Apache-2.0 with the LLVM exception; the Ace editor is BSD-3-Clause and Tree-sitter is MIT.
